before.title: 12V Auxiliary Battery Parasitic Drain / Repeated Dead Battery
before.description: Fourth-generation Outlander and Outlander PHEV owners (2022+) report the 12V auxiliary battery repeatedly going flat, sometimes leaving the car dead in a day or two, even on nearly new vehicles and with the traction battery fully charged. Identified culprits on owner forums include the OEM infotainment/radio head unit failing to fully sleep, a driver's seat control module intermittently drawing current, a WiFi/telematics module, and a charging logic that tops up the 12V battery on a fixed daily timer rather than by voltage - so a low battery may never recover. Distinct from the high-voltage traction-battery issues.
before.solution: Diagnose parasitic draw with a multimeter (fuse-pull method) to isolate the offending circuit; check for infotainment/seat-module software updates at the dealer. Replace a degraded 12V battery (vented AGM type on PHEV) and verify DC-DC/alternator charging. Some owners fit a battery maintainer for vehicles parked for extended periods. Dealers have addressed specific VINs with module reprogramming.
symptoms: Dead 12V battery / no-start after sitting 1-2 days
No dash lights, vehicle won't power on
Repeated battery replacements not fixing the drain
Infotainment or seat module suspected of not sleeping
Battery drains even shortly after full charge (PHEV)

proposal.title: 12V Auxiliary Battery Parasitic Drain / Repeated Dead Battery
proposal.description: Mitsubishi TSB-24-54-002 documents a discharged auxiliary-battery condition only on certain 2023-2024 Outlander Plug-in Hybrid vehicles. It changes PHEV-ECU charge-stopping logic under low drive-battery state of charge and updates IPDM and BCM configuration. It does not establish the frozen 2022-2024 gasoline-and-PHEV population, a one-to-two-day recurrence, or infotainment, seat, Wi-Fi and telematics modules as universal parasitic-draw causes. A weak battery, charging fault and key-off draw remain distinct paths.
proposal.solution: Identify gasoline versus PHEV configuration, VIN, battery specification and software history. Load-test the 12V battery, verify alternator or DC-DC charging, and measure key-off current only after every network has completed its prescribed sleep period; then isolate the active circuit without repeatedly waking modules. On an applicable 2023-2024 PHEV, follow TSB-24-54-002 for PHEV-ECU and configuration updates. Do not buy an AGM battery, infotainment unit, seat module, telematics module, maintainer or DC-DC converter from this page; the exact population and failed battery, charging, software or draw path must be proven first.
symptoms: gasoline or PHEV configuration and VIN verified
battery capacity and charging voltage measured
sleep-state key-off current and responsible circuit documented
affectedSystems: vehicle networks and key-off electrical loads

before.title: AC Compressor Failure
before.description: The AC compressor in the Outlander is prone to premature failure, with the internal clutch bearing seizing or the compressor developing internal leaks. Failure typically occurs between 60,000 and 90,000 miles, leaving the vehicle without air conditioning.
before.solution: Replace the AC compressor, receiver/drier, and expansion valve as a complete system. Flush the AC lines to remove debris from the failed compressor. Use the correct PAG oil specification for the replacement unit.
symptoms: AC blowing warm air
Clicking or grinding from compressor
Intermittent cooling
Refrigerant leak detected

proposal.title: AC Compressor Failure
proposal.description: The reviewed 845-row exact Outlander and Outlander PHEV manufacturer-communication corpus contains no record establishing recurring A/C compressor clutch-bearing seizure, internal compressor leakage, a 60,000-90,000-mile failure range or one 2007-2020 population. Communication 10244845 is only a 2018-2020 PHEV service-manual correction for compressor oil refill quantity; it does not prove compressor failure or authorize replacing the receiver/drier and expansion valve. Gasoline and PHEV compressor architectures and refrigerants cannot be combined without exact identification.
proposal.solution: Identify model year, powertrain, refrigerant, compressor type and high-voltage safety requirements. Do not buy a compressor, receiver/drier, expansion valve, refrigerant, oil or flush kit from this page; the exact system, failed component, contamination state and compatible materials must be proven first.

before.title: CVT Transmission Premature Failure
before.description: The Jatco CVT in the Outlander is prone to premature failure, particularly under heavy loads and in hot climates. The CVT belt and pulleys wear prematurely, leading to slipping, shuddering, and eventual complete transmission failure, often between 60,000 and 100,000 miles.
before.solution: Change CVT fluid every 30,000 miles using Mitsubishi DiaQueen CVTF-J4. Avoid aggressive driving and towing near maximum capacity. If the CVT fails, replacement with a remanufactured unit is more cost-effective than rebuild.
symptoms: Transmission shuddering during acceleration
Loss of power at highway speeds
Whining noise increasing with speed
CVT overheating warning

proposal.title: CVT Transmission Premature Failure
proposal.description: Mitsubishi TSB-20-23-001 documents a complaint-driven shudder or surge diagnostic path on certain 2016-2020 Outlander CVT-8 vehicles; under that bounded condition, repeated belt slip can place abrasion powder in the hydraulic circuit. Recall 16V563000 separately addresses a 2016 control-software acceleration delay. Other exact records cover pressure-table corrections, cooler-hose leakage and service procedures. They do not establish universal 2007-2020 premature failure, heavy-load or hot-climate causation, a 60,000-100,000-mile range or one fixed 30,000-mile service interval.
proposal.solution: Identify the installed transmission, VIN, software and recall history and exact complaint. For an applicable CVT-8 shudder or surge, follow the bulletin's test-drive, drive-data, hydraulic and belt-inspection sequence; separately check specified fluid and level, cooler and hoses, electrical control and 16V563000 completion. Do not buy CVT fluid, a cooler, valve body, belt-and-pulley assembly or remanufactured transmission from this page; the exact population, service requirement and failed software, hydraulic or mechanical path must be proven first.

before.title: Engine Malfunction / 'Power Reduced' Warning from ECU Software (False P0401/P0404, TSB-22-13-001)
before.description: Early 2022 Outlanders with the 2.5L engine can illuminate the check-engine light and display an 'Engine malfunction / Power reduced — service now' message while idling or driving, often storing EGR-related codes (P0401/P0404) that do not reflect an actual hardware fault. Mitsubishi traced this to engine-ECU control software and issued TSB-22-13-001 to reflash the ECU with countermeasure software on vehicles built before December 16, 2021.
before.solution: Have the dealer reprogram the engine ECU per Mitsubishi TSB-22-13-001 (perform the reflash first, then re-diagnose only if codes persist). The update corrects the false low-EGR-flow detection so the warning and limp-mode no longer trigger spuriously.

before.title: Fuel Pump Failure Causing Engine Stall (Recall 22V027)
before.description: NHTSA recall 22V027 (Mitsubishi campaign SR-22-001) covers ~16,600 2022 Outlanders whose in-tank fuel pump has a commutator and internal wires that may be fused incorrectly during manufacturing, causing the pump to fail. A failing fuel pump can starve the engine and cause an unexpected stall while driving, raising crash risk. This is a manufacturing/supplier defect, separate from any CVT-related stall concern.
before.solution: Check the VIN against NHTSA recall 22V027 (Mitsubishi SR-22-001 fuel pump campaign) and have the dealer replace the defective fuel pump free of charge. Warning signs of an impending failure include hard starting, sputtering, or loss of power under acceleration.
symptoms: Engine stalls or shuts off while driving
Hard starting or extended cranking
Sputtering or hesitation under acceleration
Sudden loss of power

before.title: Hood Flutter and Bounce at Highway Speed (Latch/Weatherstrip Defect)
before.description: 4th-gen Outlander owners report the hood visibly flutters, shakes, and bounces at highway speed or in strong headwinds, feeling as though it could unlatch and fly open. The defect stems from the hood-latch/bumper-stop design and weatherstripping; Mitsubishi issued a TSB (latch/bumper-stop adjustment, weatherstrip and later reinforced-hood replacement) that owners report did not reliably resolve it, and a class-action lawsuit over the defect proceeded and reached a preliminary settlement.
before.solution: Have the dealer perform the Mitsubishi hood TSB (hood-latch and bumper-stop adjustment, weatherstrip replacement, and in later revisions a reinforced-hood replacement). If flutter persists, document it with NHTSA and check eligibility under the Outlander hood-defect class-action settlement, since the published fix was widely reported as incomplete.
symptoms: Hood shakes or flutters at 50+ mph
Hood bounces in strong headwinds or over bumps
Visible gap or movement at the leading edge of the hood
Sensation the hood could pop open while driving

before.title: Phantom / False Automatic Emergency Braking (Forward Collision Mitigation)
before.description: Multiple NHTSA complaints describe the Outlander's Forward Collision Mitigation system warning and applying hard automatic braking with no obstacle present, including a 2022 SEL that decelerated from 70 mph and another that slowed itself without driver input. False triggers occur on highway curves and in rain or heavy dew that confuse the radar/camera sensors, creating rear-end collision risk.
before.solution: Update the ADAS/FCM software at the dealer and have the front radar and windshield-mounted camera inspected, cleaned, and recalibrated. Drivers can temporarily disable Forward Collision Mitigation where false activations are dangerous, but a software update/recalibration is the proper remedy.
symptoms: Automatic emergency braking with no vehicle ahead
Sudden hard braking on open highway or curves
False collision warnings in rain or heavy dew
System misreads vehicles in adjacent lanes as directly ahead

before.title: Spontaneous Windshield and Door Glass Cracking (4th-Gen Thin Glass)
before.description: Fourth-generation Outlander (2022+, GN platform shared with Nissan Rogue) owners report windshields and side door glass cracking spontaneously or from minor road impacts, often within the first weeks of ownership. NHTSA complaints and CarComplaints entries describe cracks appearing with no visible rock strike, including glass cracking while the vehicle sits in a driveway, and multiple owners describe the OEM glass as thin/'cheap.' Because the windshield houses the forward camera for Forward Collision Mitigation and lane assist, replacement requires ADAS recalibration, driving cost well above a standard windshield.
before.solution: No recall or TSB addresses the glass quality; replacement is the only fix. Owners use insurance/comprehensive glass coverage. Aftermarket OEM-equivalent windshields plus mandatory ADAS camera recalibration; some owners report better durability with aftermarket laminated glass. Document repeat cracks for potential goodwill/lemon claims.
symptoms: Windshield crack appears with no known impact
Long cracks spreading from edge of glass
Front driver or passenger door glass cracking while driving
Crack appearing within first weeks of ownership
Stress cracks originating near the frit/edge band

proposal.title: Spontaneous Windshield and Door Glass Cracking (4th-Gen Thin Glass)
proposal.description: The reviewed exact 2022-2025 Outlander manufacturer-communication and recall corpora contain no record establishing spontaneous windshield or door-glass cracking, thin or cheap OEM glass, a shared-platform defect or one fourth-generation population. Communication 10175776 only updates windshield removal and installation cautions for ADAS-equipped 2014-2020 vehicles and does not prove cracking. An absent visible impact mark does not by itself distinguish impact, edge damage, installation stress, body movement, temperature stress or a manufacturing defect.
proposal.solution: Photograph the entire crack, origin, edges and surrounding body before repair and have a qualified glass specialist inspect for impact, edge damage, installation stress and body-opening damage. Verify the exact glass specification, sensors and required camera calibration under the vehicle procedure; preserve repeated-failure documentation for warranty or insurance review. Do not buy a windshield, door glass, moulding, adhesive or calibration service from this page; the exact glass, damage cause, installation materials and ADAS requirement must be proven first.

before.title: Front Suspension Clunking and Noise
before.description: The Outlander develops front suspension clunking and knocking noises over bumps and rough roads. Worn front stabilizer bar end links and strut mount bearings are the primary culprits, with noise appearing as early as 30,000 miles.
before.solution: Replace the front stabilizer bar end links and strut mounts. Inspect the lower control arm bushings while the suspension is apart. OEM replacement parts are recommended as some aftermarket components have fitment issues.
symptoms: Clunking over bumps
Knocking noise during turns
Rattling from front suspension
Noise worse on rough roads

proposal.title: Front Suspension Clunking and Noise
proposal.description: Mitsubishi TSB-23-33-002REV3 documents creaking or popping from a deformed front strut-bearing support only on certain 2022-2024 Outlander vehicles while the steering wheel is turned. It directs replacement of the noisy side's strut bearing and front spring with countermeasure parts. That bounded condition does not establish bump-related clunking, stabilizer end-link and strut-mount failure, a 30,000-mile onset or one 2014-2026 population. Other exact records are inspection and service-manual corrections rather than recurrence proof.
proposal.solution: Identify model year, VIN and the exact condition that reproduces the noise. Separate steering-at-rest strut-bearing noise from bump, brake, stabilizer, ball-joint, control-arm, mount, spring, damper, wheel-bearing and driveline paths using loaded inspection and the applicable service procedure. For an applicable 2022-2024 steering-related complaint, follow TSB-23-33-002REV3. Do not buy end links, strut mounts, bearings, springs, dampers or control arms from this page; the exact population, noise source and failed component must be proven first.
symptoms: VIN and noise condition verified
steering-related noise separated from bump and brake noise
loaded bearing, spring, link, joint, bushing and mount findings documented
affectedSystems: stabilizer links, joints and control-arm bushings
brakes, wheel bearings, mounts and driveline noise paths
